fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time discrimination of a HAWK display amid background clutter is a substantive, well-recognized signal-conspicuity safety issue with direct consequences for stopping behavior over a pedestrian crossing at final design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal driver-confusion claim is supported by a verbatim quoted site-specific observation (EV-US-001, TABLE A.10 Issue 6); the driver-risk-to-pedestrian link is honestly flagged as inference rather than invented fact.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a safety_concern with no normative_basis_note, keeping the conspicuity/safety question categorically distinct from any MUTCD compliance assertion under FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: A retroreflective border/backplate treatment is specific, actionable, viable at final design, and directly targets detection/discrimination against background clutter.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the exposed VRUs if drivers misread or detect the beacon late—are explicitly identified and the scenario ties driver conspicuity to their protection.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance interval adequacy for slower walkers at high-collision-frequency HAWK sites is a genuine, mechanistically described safety exposure still correctable at final design stage.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is backed by a verbatim quoted passage (EV-US-016) matching the recorded TABLE A.10 issue for these exact sites, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern with a verify-style audit question under us-fhwa:final-design, with no conflation into MUTCD compliance assertions.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific (all six sites), actionable (reprogramme with reduced assumed walking speed), and viable within final-design signal timing changes; not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians explicitly named as affected road users and their still-clearing exposure is the core of the finding, so VRU impact is fully considered.
